event/delegation-of-hamdan: The delegation and mission to Hamdan
event/delegation-of-kinda: Al-Ash'ath ibn Qays comes with the delegation of Kinda
event/delegation-of-tayy: Zayd al-Khayl comes with the delegation of Tayy
The delegation of Tayy came with their chief Zayd al-Khayl; the Prophet offered them Islam and they became good Muslims.
event/demolition-of-al-uzza-and-idols: The Demolition of al-Uzza and Major Idols
event/demolition-of-husayn-tomb: Demolition of the tomb of al-Husayn

event/deposition-abd-al-hamid-1327: Deposition of Sultan Abd al-Hamid II
event/djinguereber-built-1327: On Mansa Musa's return from the hajj the Andalusian architect Abu Ishaq al-Sahili came with him and built the Djinguereber mosque at Timbuktu about 1327 .
event/duel-of-amr-ibn-abd-wudd: Ali's duel with Amr ibn Abd Wudd at the Trench
At the Battle of the Trench, enemy horsemen forced a breach in the ditch.
event/edirne-eski-saray-767: Murad I builds the Old Palace at Edirne
event/edirne-fire-1158: Edirne's decline was hastened by the fire of 1158/1745, in which some sixty quarters of the city were burnt down, followed by the earthquake of 1164/1751 .
event/egypt-earthquakes-272: News reached Baghdad in Jumada I 272 that Egypt had been shaken by earthquakes that ruined houses and the congregational mosque, with a thousand funerals counted in a single day .
event/egypt-fleet-acre-587: Egypt army and fleet reach the Acre theater
Egypt field army and its fleet arrived at Acre to reinforce Saladin against the crusader besiegers .
event/eighth-crusade-tunis-669: Louis IX's siege of Tunis (the Eighth Crusade)
event/emigration-of-the-companions: The emigration of the Muslims to Yathrib after the pledge
event/end-umayyad-caliphate-cordoba-424: End of the Umayyad caliphate at Cordoba
Hisham al-Mu'tadd, the last Umayyad caliph of Cordoba, was deposed; the Andalusi kings dropped the Marwanid caliphate and the taifa rulers rose.
event/erbil-mosul-siege-621: Muzaffar al-Din of Irbil besieges Mosul
Muzaffar al-Din Kokburi of Irbil besieged Mosul, then withdrew .
event/eski-cami-edirne-804: Edirne's Eski Cami (Old Mosque) is built
Emir Süleyman, son of Bayezid I, began Edirne's Eski Cami in 804/1402 during the interregnum, and Mehmed I completed it in 816/1413 .
event/euphrates-flood-329: The Euphrates flood and the ruin of Bab al-Anbar
event/expedition-of-al-abwa-waddan: The first expedition led personally by the Prophet in Safar 2 AH with 70 Muhajirun; established an alliance treaty with Amr ibn Makhshi of Banu Damra.
event/expedition-of-al-kharrar: An expedition led by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas with 20 Muhajirun in Dhu al-Qada 1 AH marching on foot by night towards al-Kharrar; found the caravan had passed the day before.
event/expedition-of-al-kudr: An expedition of 200 Muslims led by the Prophet in Shawwal 2 AH to al-Kudr to disperse Banu Sulaym and Ghatafan gathering against Medina; the tribes scattered and Muslims captured 500 camels.
event/expedition-of-al-sawiq: An expedition in Dhu al-Hijjah 2 AH pursuing Abu Sufyan who raided the outskirts of Medina with 200 riders; the Meccans dumped bags of roasted barley flour (sawiq) to lighten their load during flight.
event/expedition-of-banu-al-nadir: The Siege and Expulsion of Banu al-Nadir
event/expedition-of-buhran: An expedition led by the Prophet with 300 men in Rabi' al-Thani 3 AH to Buhran in the direction of al-Furu'; stayed through Jumada al-Ula without encounter.
event/expedition-of-buwat: An expedition led by the Prophet in Rabi' al-Awwal 2 AH with 200 companions to intercept a Quraysh caravan led by Umayya ibn Khalaf; reached Mount Buwat without encounter.
event/expedition-of-dhu-al-ushayra: An expedition led by the Prophet in Jumada al-Ula/al-Akhirah 2 AH with 150-200 Muhajirun to intercept a Quraysh caravan to Sham (the caravan pursued later at Badr); concluded a treaty with Banu Mudlij.
event/expedition-of-dhu-amarr: An expedition led by the Prophet with 450 men in Muharram 3 AH to disperse Banu Thalaba and Muharib at Dhu Amarr; the Bedouins fled to mountain tops without fighting.
event/expedition-of-dhu-qarad: The Expedition of Dhu Qarad (Ghazwat al-Ghaba)
event/expedition-of-safwan: An expedition led by the Prophet in Rabi' al-Awwal 2 AH in pursuit of Kurz ibn Jabir al-Fihri after he raided the pastures of Medina; chased him to the valley of Safwan near Badr.
event/expedition-of-sif-al-bahr: The first expedition dispatched by the Prophet, led by Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib with 30 Muhajirun in Ramadan 1 AH to intercept a Quraysh caravan; mediated by Majdi ibn Amr without clash.
event/fall-of-acre-587: The Franks take Acre and kill the captives
On Friday, 17 Jumada II 587, the Franks took Acre after a long siege.
event/fall-of-algeciras-744: The fall of al-Jazira al-Khadra and the breaking of the fleet
event/fall-of-cordoba-636: The Castilian capture of Cordoba on Sunday 23 Shawwal 636, within the reconquest register that took Zaragoza in 512, Murcia by treaty 643 and Seville 646 .
event/fall-of-granada-897: The surrender of Granada and the Christian entry into the Alhambra
Boabdil, the last Nasrid sultan, formally surrendered Granada to the Catholic Monarchs on 2 January 1492, 2 Rabi I 897, ending the Nasrid kingdom.
event/fall-of-seville-646: The fall of Seville by treaty
Seville was besieged in 645 and surrendered to the Castilian on Monday 5 Sha'ban 646 after about seventeen months of investment .
event/fall-of-valencia-636: The fall of Valencia to the enemy
Valencia fell by treaty on 17 Safar 636 after Ibn al-Abbar's plea-qasida to the Hafsid sultan moved him to ship money and supplies; its people surrendered on terms preserving their persons in 637 .
event/fall-of-zaragoza-512: Saragossa fell to the Christians on Wednesday 4 Ramadan 512 — the capital of the Upper March passing out of Muslim hands .
event/false-alid-claimant-302: The claimant to descent from al-Rida the Alid
In Dhu'l-Qa'da 302 a man was brought before al-Muqtadir claiming descent from al-Rida the Alid; unmasked as a son of al-Dab'i, he was paraded on both sides of the city and jailed .
event/farewell-pilgrimage: The only pilgrimage the Prophet led, during which he gave the sermon known as the Farewell Sermon.
event/farewell-visit-to-uhud-martyrs: The farewell prayer over the martyrs of Uhud
event/fasting-of-ramadan-prescribed: The prescription of the Ramadan fast
The fast of the month of Ramadan was prescribed for the Muslims of Medina in the second year after the Hijra.
event/fath-mecca-cleansing-kaaba: The cleansing of the Kaaba and destruction of idols
event/fath-mecca-sermon: The Prophet's sermon at the Kaaba and general amnesty
event/fatima-inheritance-claim-fadak: Fatima's claim to the Prophet's inheritance and Fadak
After the Prophet's death Fatima and al-Abbas asked Abu Bakr for their share of the Prophet's estate, the land of Fadak and his share of Khaybar.
event/fatimid-conquest-of-egypt-358: Jawhar's conquest of Egypt and the laying out of Cairo
In 357 the Qarmatians took Damascus and meant for Egypt — the Ubaydids took it first.
event/fatimid-dinar-ban-427: Al-Qadir bans dealing in Maghrebi dinars
event/first-encounter-with-the-ansar: First encounter with the six Ansar at al-Aqaba
event/first-jumua-yathrib: The first Friday prayer in Yathrib
event/first-raid-on-sicily: The First Raid on Sicily and Abdallah ibn Qays's Plunder
In al-Baladhuri: Mu'awiya ibn Khudayj al-Kindi raided Sicily in Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan's days — the first to raid it — and it kept being raided thereafter.
event/flight-of-ubaydallah-ibn-ziyad-fro: Ubaydallah ibn Ziyad's flight from Basra after Yazid's death
event/founding-of-marrakesh-1070: The Almoravid amir Yusuf ibn Tashfin ordered Marrakesh built in 462/1070; it became the Almoravid capital .
event/founding-of-shahjahanabad-1638: In 1638 Shah Jahan ordered a new walled capital at Delhi, named Shahjahanabad, with the Red Fort at its heart .
event/franks-armenians-fitna-623: Strife between the Franks and the Armenians
Strife broke out between the Franks and the Armenians on the Syrian marches .
event/franks-constantinople-601: In 601 the Franks seized Constantinople and expelled the Romans — theirs since before Islam — and held it till 660, when the Romans took it back .
event/franks-damietta-616: The Franks Take Damietta and the Founding of al-Mansura
In 615 the Franks took Damietta's chain-tower — 'the lock of Egypt's lands', says Abu Shama, a tall tower mid-Nile with two chains barring the salt sea to ships.
event/franks-sham-raid-600: Frankish seaborne raid on the coast and the truce
Large Frankish fleets reached the Syrian coast while the Muslim armies were consumed by the succession wars; a truce followed .
event/franks-sham-raids-606: Frankish raids recurred on the Syrian coast and ports while the sultans fought one another .
event/franks-sidon-625: Frankish expedition to Syria; Sidon refortified
A Frankish expedition reached Syria and rebuilt Sidon's defenses while the Muslims were divided .
event/franks-syria-egypt-614: The Franks appear in Syria and march on Egypt
The Franks came out to Syria then marched on Egypt — the opening move of the great Damietta war .
event/franks-tripoli-503: The Franks Take Tripoli of Syria
event/french-occupation-algiers-1246: France seized Algiers in 1830 with some 28,000 troops and a hundred-ship fleet while the caliphate was weakened — European powers endorsing it as the first share-out of the 'sick man's' estate .
event/fuwwa-raid-601: Frankish fleet sacks Fuwwa on the Egyptian coast
A Frankish fleet entered Egyptian waters and sacked Fuwwa, killing and capturing its people .
event/georgians-armenia-604: Georgians plunder Armenia from the Khilat side
The Georgians came in force into the Khilat region of Armenia, plundering, killing and taking captives .
event/georgians-azerbaijan-raid-601: The Georgians raided the Islamic lands from the Azerbaijan side, ravaging, killing and plundering .
event/georgians-baylaqan-619: The Georgians sacked Baylaqan in Arran, razing it and slaughtering its people .
event/georgians-ganja-622: The Georgians besieged Ganja in Arran and pressed its people hard .
event/georgians-routed-622: Jalal al-Din routed the Georgians in Azerbaijan with great slaughter and captives .
event/georgians-tiflis-624: The Georgians enter and burn Tiflis
The Georgians entered and burned Tiflis after its people defected from Jalal al-Din and called them in .
event/ghadir-khumm: A halt at the pool of Khumm on the return from the Farewell Pilgrimage, at which the Prophet spoke about Ali.
event/ghar-thawr: The three nights in the cave of Thawr
event/ghassan-kings-letter-to-kaab: The letter of the king of Ghassan to Ka'b ibn Malik
event/ghiyath-leaves-karramiyya-596: Ghiyath al-Din al-Ghuri quits the Karramiyya
event/ghiyath-mahmud-ghuri-killed-605: Ghiyath al-Din Mahmud of Ghur was killed and the Ghurid realm fell into disorder until the Khwarazmians took most of it .
event/ghuzz-sack-mosul-435: The Ghuzz enter Mosul and plunder Qarwash's palace
event/greek-landing-izmir-1338: The Greek landing at Izmir (1919), enabled by Britain, and Mustafa Kemal's counter-campaign that drove them out and won him the title Ghazi across the Muslim world .
event/greek-occupation-edirne-1920: After the Balkan Wars Edirne fell briefly under Bulgarian occupation in 1913, then was occupied by the Greeks between 1920 and 1922, and has since been a Turkish frontier city .
event/habib-armenia-circuit: Habib ibn Maslama's Circuit of Armenia
event/hafsid-independence-627: Abu Zakariya al-Hafsi's break with the Almohads
event/hajj-led-by-abu-bakr: The pilgrimage led by Abu Bakr
The Prophet sent Abu Bakr to lead the pilgrimage of the ninth year after the Hijra, the first led by the Muslims after the conquest of Mecca.
event/hakim-women-confinement-405: Al-Hakim Forbids the Women of Egypt to Go Out
event/hawazin-delegation-and-amnesty: The Hawazin delegation and the amnesty of captives
event/herzl-audience-1901: Herzl's Audience with Sultan Abdulhamid II
event/hijra-departure: The departure night of the Hijra
event/hilali-into-ifriqiya-440: The First Entry of the Arab Tribes into Ifriqiya
event/hilf-al-fudul: Hilf al-Fudul (the pact of the virtuous)
event/hypocrites-discourage-marching-in-: Some say: do not march in the heat
event/hypocrites-mock-the-army-and-excus: A group of hypocrites mock the army, then excuse themselves
event/ibadi-imamate-oman-51: The Ibadi imamate rises in Oman
The Ibadi imamate rose in Oman about 51/671, settling Muscat and the coast under its imams .
event/ibadi-revolt-oman-134: The Ibadi revolt of al-Julanda in Oman
The Ibadi rising of al-Julanda ibn Mas'ud in Oman, crushed by al-Saffah's general Khazim ibn Khuzayma with some ten thousand dead, 134 AH .
event/ibn-al-haytham-summoned-to-cairo: The Fatimid caliph al-Ḥākim summoned Ibn al-Haytham from Basra to Egypt to devise a regulation of the Nile flood; seeing the task impossible he feigned madness until al-Ḥākim's death in 1021 .
event/ibn-al-zubayr-rebuilds-kaba: Ibn al-Zubayr's rebuilding of the Ka'ba
event/ibn-battuta-completes-hajj-1326: Ibn Battuta completes his first pilgrimage
In 1326 Ibn Battuta completed the pilgrimage, having come through Egypt and Syria with a caravan to Mecca; he then crossed the desert to Iraq.
event/ibn-battuta-envoy-to-china-1342: Ibn Battuta named envoy to China
In 1342 the Delhi sultan Muhammad ibn Tughluq appointed Ibn Battuta his envoy to the Chinese emperor, after years at his court.
event/ibn-battuta-returns-to-fez-1349: In November 1349 Ibn Battuta reached Fez, capital of the Marinid sultan Abu Inan, after sailing from Alexandria to Tunisia, Sardinia and Algiers.
event/ibn-hazm-birth-cordoba-384: Ibn Hazm is born in the Munyat al-Mughira quarter of Cordoba
Abu Muhammad Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Hazm was born in the Munyat al-Mughira quarter of Cordoba on the last day of Ramadan, 384 AH.
event/ibn-hazm-death-in-exile-456: Ibn Hazm dies in exile in the desert of Labla
Ibn Hazm died in the desert village of Mant Lisham, in the district of Labla, on the evening of a Sunday two nights before the end of Sha'ban, 456 AH, after rulers had driven him from his homeland.
event/ibn-jawzi-nahrawani-madrasas-556: Ibn al-Jawzi succeeds Abu Hakim al-Nahrawani in his two madrasas
event/ibn-jubayr-baghdad-580: Ibn Jubayr stayed at Baghdad describing the Nizamiyya college, the quarter of Abd al-Qadir and its markets .
event/ibn-jubayr-departs-granada-578: Ibn Jubayr sets out from Granada
In Safar 578/1183 Ibn Jubayr left Granada for the hajj, crossing the sea by way of Ceuta and the west .
event/ibn-jubayr-in-alexandria-578: Ibn Jubayr reached Alexandria — its lighthouse, its colleges, the dar al-adl and Sultan Saladin .
event/ibn-jubayr-medina-580: Ibn Jubayr visited Medina describing the Prophet's mosque, the tomb, the Rawda and Quba .
event/ibn-jubayr-palermo-580: The ship carrying Ibn Jubayr was wrecked off Sicily; King William II rescued the passengers and he landed at Palermo .
event/ibn-jubayr-returns-granada-581: Ibn Jubayr returned to Granada in 581/1185 after two years' travel and wrote his rihla, the Tadhkira .
event/ibn-khaldun-court-tunis-1352: Ibn Khaldun receives a post at the court of Tunis
Around 1352, at about the age of twenty, Ibn Khaldun was given a post at the court of Tunis; three years later he became secretary to the Marinid sultan in Fez.
event/ibn-khaldun-parents-die-black-deat: The Black Death takes Ibn Khaldun's parents in Tunis
In 1349 the Black Death struck Tunis and took both of Ibn Khaldun's parents.
event/ibn-khurmail-killed-605: Ibn Khurmail killed; Herat besieged again
Ibn Khurmail was killed and Herat besieged anew; Khwarazmshah himself was captured on the march and freed .
event/ibn-layun-aleppo-raids-604: Ibn Layun the Armenian raids the Aleppo countryside
Ibn Layun the Armenian, lord of the Passes, launched repeated raids on Aleppo's territories .
event/ibn-sina-leaves-for-gurgan-1012: Ibn Sina travels west to Gorgan
In 1012 Ibn Sina left Khwarazm and travelled west through the cities of Khurasan towards Gorgan (Jurjan).
event/ibn-sina-service-at-rayy-1014: Ibn Sina enters Buyid service at Rayy
In about 1014 Ibn Sina went to Rayy and entered the service of the Buyid amir Majd al-Dawla and his mother Sayyida Shirin as court physician.
event/ibn-sina-to-khuzistan-1030: In January 1030, during the brief Ghaznavid occupation of Isfahan, Ibn Sina and Ala al-Dawla moved to Khuzistan, staying until the death of Mahmud of Ghazna two months later.
event/ibn-sina-vizier-hamadan-1015: Ibn Sina becomes vizier to Shams al-Dawla at Hamadan
In 1015, at Hamadan, Ibn Sina passed into the service of the Buyid amir Shams al-Dawla, who made him his vizier; he held the post until Shams al-Dawla died in 1021.
event/ibn-ubayy-separate-camp-and-withdr: Ibn Ubayy's separate camp and his staying behind
Abdullah ibn Ubayy pitched his own camp below the Prophet's camp toward Dhubab — as they claim, no smaller than the Prophet's own.
event/ibrahim-abbasiyya-founding: Ibrahim ibn al-Aghlab's Founding of al-Abbasiyya
In al-Baladhuri: when the frontier army besieged Ibrahim at Qayrawan, al-Muradi and al-Mamrun came to him bearing money from Egypt's kharaj — when paid, they dispersed.
event/idris-ii-founds-fes-193: Idris ibn Idris built the city of Fez on the two banks of its wadi in 193/808, making it the capital of the Maghreb .
event/ildigiz-rayy-566: Shams al-Dīn Īldigiz, atabeg of Azerbaijan, took al-Rayy — won through the vizier Ibn ʿArabshāh al-Ibrāhīmī — then held Azerbaijan and the Jibāl as an independent power .
event/incident-of-the-poisoned-sheep: The Incident of the Poisoned Sheep at Khaybar
event/incident-of-the-slander: The Incident of the Slander (Hadith al-Ifk)

event/ismail-berber-dawah: Isma'il ibn Abdallah and Umar II's Mission to the Berbers
event/jafar-arrival-at-khaybar: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib comes before the Prophet at Khaybar
event/jalal-al-dawla-restored-418: The restoration of the khutba to Jalal al-Dawla in Baghdad
In 418 the Baghdad crowd pressed the caliph until Abu Kalijar was deposed and the khutba was restored to Jalal al-Dawla Abu Tahir .
event/jalal-amid-628: Jalal al-Din reaches Amid and is routed there
Jalal al-Din reached Amid and was utterly routed by the Mongols; Ibn al-Athir reports a merchant's estimate of more than fifteen thousand Muslim dead .
event/jalal-ani-qars-623: Jalal al-Din besieges Ani and Kars
Jalal al-Din besieged Ani and Kars in the Georgian lands .
event/jalal-armenia-625: Jalal al-Din plundered Armenia so hard that ruin spread across it .
event/jalal-azerbaijan-622: Jalal al-Din took Azerbaijan after defeating its ruler Uzbak and entered Tabriz .
event/jalal-khilat-626: Jalal al-Din besieges and takes Khilat
Jalal al-Din besieged Khilat until he took it — his greatest prize in the Rum-Armenian marches .
event/jalal-khilat-siege-623: Jalal al-Din's first siege of Khilat
Jalal al-Din besieged Khilat hard and withdrew — he returned and took it in 626 .
event/jalal-khuzistan-iraq-622: Jalal al-Din reaches Khuzistan and Iraq
Jalal al-Din, fresh from defeat by the Mongols, reached Khuzistan and Iraq and gathered a new army .
event/jalali-calendar-reform-467: Sultan Malik-Shah charged Umar Khayyam and a team of astronomers with reforming the calendar; at the Isfahan observatory they produced the Jalali calendar about 467/1079 .
event/jalaluddin-takes-tiflis-623: Jalal al-Din takes the city of Tiflis from the Georgians
On 8 Rabi' I 623 Jalal al-Din b.
event/jama-masjid-delhi-completed-1656: Completion of the Jama Masjid of Delhi
The Jama Masjid of Shahjahanabad — the largest mosque of India, built on Shah Jahan's order — was completed in 1656 .
event/janissary-mutiny-edirne-850: Murad II's reign saw a janissary mutiny at Edirne on the pretext of the fire that had broken out in the city; the soldiery rioted until the rising was pacified by an increase in their pay .
event/jaqmaq-accession-842: Deposition of al-Aziz and accession of Jaqmaq
In 842 the amirs deposed al-Aziz Yusuf ibn Barsbay after a sultanate of three months and installed al-Zahir Abu Sa'id Jaqmaq in his place .
event/jerusalem-thunderbolt-851: In mid-Shawwal 851 a tremendous thunderbolt struck Jerusalem .
event/jinn-hear-the-quran: A company of jinn hear the Qur'an at Wadi Nakhla
event/kaab-and-abu-qatada-at-the-garden-: Ka'b and Abu Qatada at the garden wall
During the boycott Ka'b climbed the wall of his cousin Abu Qatada's garden and greeted him; he did not answer.
event/kaab-ibn-malik-delays-his-preparat: Ka'b ibn Malik puts off his preparations for Tabuk
event/kaab-ibn-zuhayr-pardon-and-burda: Ka'b ibn Zuhayr's pardon and recitation of Banat Su'ad
event/kaab-offers-his-wealth-and-vows-tr: Ka'b offers his wealth and vows to speak only the truth
event/kaab-tells-the-prophet-the-truth: Ka'b tells the Prophet the truth
When news of the Prophet's return from Tabuk reached Ka'b he resolved on honesty.
event/kabul-revolt-yazid-death: Kabul's Breach and Yazid ibn Ziyad's Death
event/kalenderoglu-plunders-bursa-1017: Jelali bands threatened Bursa from 1003/1595, and in 1017/1608 Kalenderoğlu came to plunder the city .
event/kamil-hama-626: al-Kamil took Hama and added it to his Syrian holdings .
event/karamanid-siege-bursa-1413: The Karamanid Turcoman emir besieged Bursa in 1413 CE and destroyed the Orhan Gazi Mosque; the mosque was repaired four years later .
event/karkh-qalain-gates-441: The gate-building war between Karkh and al-Qala'in
event/kayqubad-amid-623: War between Kayqubad and the lord of Amid
War ran between Kayqubad I of Rum and the Artuqid lord of Amid .
event/khalid-expedition-to-ukaydir: Khalid's mission to Ukaydir of Dumat al-Jandal
The Prophet summoned Khalid ibn al-Walid and sent him to Ukaydir ibn Abd al-Malik al-Kindi, the Christian king of Duma, telling him he would find him hunting wild cows.
event/khalid-kills-ukaydir: Khalid Kills Ukaydir and Takes Dumat al-Jandal
event/khayyam-algebra-treatise: About 1070 Umar Khayyam composed his treatise on the demonstration of problems of algebra, solving cubic equations with conic sections .
event/khosrow-derbent-wall: Anushirwan's Building of the Bab wa-l-Abwab Wall
event/khwarazm-ghazna-611: Khwarazmshah takes Ghazna and its dependencies
Khwarazmshah took Ghazna and its dependencies after the Ghurid hold on them ended .
event/khwarazm-herat-siege-600: Muhammad Khwarazmshah besieged Herat in Rajab 600 — his first move into Ghurid Khurasan after Tekish's death — then withdrew .
event/khwarazm-kerman-makran-sind-609: Khwarazmshah takes Kirman, Makran and Sind
Khwarazmshah took Kirman, Makran and Sind — his realm now stretched from Iraq to India .
event/khwarazm-transoxiana-605: Khwarazmshah takes Transoxiana and restores Khurasan
Muhammad Khwarazmshah took Transoxiana while restoring order to a Khurasan torn by feuds since Shihab al-Din's death .
event/killing-aq-sunqur-bursuqi-520: In 1126 the Batinis assassinated Aq Sunqur al-Bursuqi, atabeg of Mosul and crusade-fighter, while he prayed in Mosul's Great Mosque .
event/killing-of-kulthum-ibn-iyad: The Killing of Kulthum ibn Iyad in Ifriqiya
In al-Baladhuri on Ibn al-Kalbi's report: Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik gave Kulthum ibn Iyad ibn Wahwah al-Qushayri Ifriqiya, whose people rose against him so that he was killed there.
event/killing-of-mansur-ibn-jamwana: The Killing of Mansur ibn Jamwana

event/killing-of-muhammad-ibn-abi-bakr: The Killing of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr in Egypt
event/kitab-al-manazir-composed: In Cairo Ibn al-Haytham composed the Book of Optics, his greatest work — built on experiment rather than conjecture, and it remade the science of vision into the seventeenth century .
event/konya-masud-capital-512: Mas'ud I makes Konya the Rum Seljuk capital

event/uhud-muslim-mobilization: Uhud war council and Muslim mobilization
When news of the Quraysh army heading for Medina reached the Prophet he held a senior war council.
event/uhud-tactical-deployment: Tactical Deployment of the Muslim Army at Uhud
The distribution of forces on the right and left wings, and the appointment of fifty archers on the Archers' Hill to protect the army's rear.
event/ulu-cami-bursa-1396: Bursa's Grand Mosque (Ulu Cami) is built
event/ulugh-beg-observatory-samarqand: Ulugh Beg, Timur's grandson, raised his great observatory at Samarkand about 823/1420, producing with Qadizada and Ali Qushji the Sultanic tables .
event/umar-dismisses-al-numan-ibn-adi: Umar dismisses al-Nu'man ibn Adi from Maysan
Ibn Ishaq relates that Umar ibn al-Khattab appointed al-Nu'man ibn Adi over Maysan in the Basra region, then dismissed him when verses attributed to him reached Umar.
event/uqbat-hulwan-pass-280: In 280 AH al-Mu'tadid ordered the Hulwan pass leveled at a cost of twenty thousand dinars — travelers had long suffered its hardship .
event/usurpation-cordoba-399: The Cordoba Strife and the Rising of Ibn Abd al-Jabbar
event/utba-offer: Utba ibn Rabi'a's offer to the Prophet
event/uthman-consults-on-ifriqiya: Uthman consults the Companions on the campaign to Ifriqiya
event/uthman-funds-the-army-of-hardship: Uthman funds the army of hardship
The Prophet urged the wealthy to spend and provide mounts in God's path, and men among them did.
event/uthmanic-mushaf-tiberias-damascus-: Transfer of the Uthmanic Mushaf from Tiberias to Damascus
In 493 the Uthmanic mushaf was carried from Tiberias to Damascus for fear — the people went out to receive it and it was housed in a chest in the mosque's maqsura .
event/vow-and-lot-of-abd-al-muttalib: ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib’s Vow and the Lot
His vow to sacrifice a son; the lot fell on ʿAbdullāh, and by an auguress’s counsel camels were raised to one hundred and slaughtered in his stead — fixing the Arab bloodwit at a hundred camels.
event/walid-council: al-Walid's council on how to brand the Prophet
event/waqat-al-sudan-cairo-564: The battle of the Sudan between the two palaces
event/waqf-haramayn-303: al-Muqtadir's Endowment for the Two Sanctuaries
In 303 al-Muqtadir endowed many crown revenues on the two Sanctuaries, summoning the judges and witnesses to record it against himself .
event/wasit-boats-drown-348: The Sinking of the Pilgrim Boats from Wasit
In 348 seventeen boats of pilgrims coming from Wasit sank with six hundred men, women and children aboard; that Jumada I the Shi'i–Sunni fitnas killed people and a great fire took Bab al-Taq .
event/water-of-wadi-al-mushaqqaq: On the road was a trickle of water in a valley called Wadi al-Mushaqqaq, enough only for a rider or two.
event/wazir-khuzistan-590: the caliph's vizier marches on and takes Khuzistan
Al-Nasir sent his vizier against Khuzistan and took it — the castle of Susiyan ibn Shamla falling to Baghdad when its dead lord sons quarreled and one wrote the caliph offering the keys .
event/year-of-delegations: In the ninth year after the Hijra, delegations from tribes across Arabia came to Medina to accept Islam or make agreements.
event/year-of-sorrow: The tenth year of prophethood in which the Prophet's protective uncle Abu Talib and his supportive wife Khadija bint Khuwaylid passed away within a short span.
event/year-of-the-elephant-and-birth: The Year of the Elephant and the Prophet's birth
The traditional year of the Prophet Muhammad's birth in Mecca — Monday 9 Rabi' I of the Year of the Elephant, given in the book as 20 or 22 April 571 CE.
event/yemen-mecca-620: The ruler of Yemen takes Mecca
The lord of Yemen took Mecca as the house of Qatada weakened there .
event/yesil-cami-bursa-1412: The Green Mosque and Green Tomb of Bursa
Çelebi Mehmet commissioned the Green Mosque (Yeşil Cami) in 1412 CE, the year before he became sole ruler as Mehmed I; the architect was Hacı Ivaz Pasha.
event/yildirim-bayezid-kulliye-bursa-139: The Yıldırım Bayezid külliye at Bursa
Bayezid I erected his imperial külliye on a hilltop east of central Bursa in 1390-1396 CE: a mosque with a zaviye, two medreses, an imaret, a palace and his türbe .
event/zahir-accession-622: al-Zahir bi-Amr Allah succeeds to the caliphate
al-Zahir bi-Amr Allah Muhammad ibn al-Nasir received the bay'a; he had been his father's appointed heir .
event/zahir-manbij-597: al-Zahir Ghazi takes Manbij and is besieged
Al-Zahir Ghazi ibn Saladin took Manbij and its region, was besieged in it by his Ayyubid rivals, then made peace .
event/zallaqa-504: The Great Battle Between Ibn Tashfin and the Franks
In 504 came the great melhama between the Franks and Ibn Tashfin, lord of al-Andalus: the Muslims were victorious, killed, captured and took spoil past telling, and the Franks' bravest perished .
event/zanj-wasit-264: In 264 AH the Zanj entered Wasit and emptied it — the people walked out barefoot while the rebels found houses still furnished; the town was struck with fire .
event/zanzibar-british-protectorate-1890: On 14 June 1890 Sultan Ali bin Said signed a provisional agreement with the British consul accepting the protectorate; the Arabic article dates the formal acceptance to 7 November 1890.
event/zuhayr-martyrdom-barqa: The Martyrdom of Zuhayr ibn Qays at Barqa

person/aisha-taymur: Egyptian poet and writer (1840–1902) who composed in Arabic, Turkish and Persian and is counted among the pioneers of modern Arabic women's writing.

person/akbar-hashemi-rafsanjani: Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani (1934–2017) was an Iranian Shia cleric and politician and a founding figure of the Islamic Republic.
person/akbar-ii: Akbar II (22 April 1760 – 28 September 1837) was the nineteenth Mughal emperor, a son of Shah Alam II, reigning from 1806 to 1837.
person/akram-zuaiter: Palestinian politician, diplomat and writer from Nablus (1909–1996), a founding member of the Istiqlal Party.
person/al-abadi-abd-al-qadir: Muhyi al-Din al-'Abadi, the grammarian of Mecca
person/al-abbas-ibn-al-walid-al-bayruti: Abu al-Fadl al-Abbas ibn al-Walid of Beirut, a master reciter of Syria and companion of Abd al-Hamid ibn Bakkar; born in 169 AH and died in 270 AH according to Ibn Hajar.
person/al-abbi-muhammad: A Maliki usuli scholar from the Maghrib, known for the rational sciences, memorization and rigorous editing; named after the village of Abba in Tunisia.
person/al-abhari-abu-bakr: Al-Abhari, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abd Allah
A Maliki jurist who combined the Qur'anic readings, high-grade chains of transmission and sound jurisprudence; from Abhar, between Qazvin and Zanjan.
person/al-abili-muhammad-ibn-ibrahim: Maghribi scholar of logic and the rational sciences; Ibn Khaldun attended his lessons in Tunis.
person/al-abiwardi: al-Abiwardi (408–498) — Umayyad-descended poet and genealogist, author of the celebrated alifiyya ode 'alimm in lam tusmahi'; d.
person/al-abraqawhi-ahmad: Judge of Abarquh and a Shafi'i scholar, hadith transmitter and Sufi; born in Abarquh in Fars and died in Egypt.
person/al-abshihi-muhammad-ibn-ahmad: Egyptian man of letters and author of the Mamluk period who gathered anecdotes and curiosities in his books.
person/al-abshitay-ahmad: A Cairene jurist, first Shafi'i and then Hanbali; born in Ibshit in the Gharbiya province of Egypt.
person/al-adid-fatimid: al-Adid li-Din Allah, last Ubaydid caliph
person/al-afdal-ibn-badr-al-jamali: Fatimid vizier, born about 458/1066, known as al-Afdal.
person/al-akhdari-abd-al-rahman: A Maliki jurist and versifier from the Maghrib, known for verse treatises on law and worship that were taught in the Quranic schools.
person/al-akhfash-al-asghar-ali: A Baghdadi grammarian known as al-Akhfash al-Asghar, to distinguish him from other grammarians who bore the name.
person/al-akwa-muhammad-ibn-ali: A scholar of jurisprudence and inheritance law, philologist and prolific writer, with wide knowledge of the history of Yemen in the Islamic period.
person/al-albani-muhammad-nasir-al-din: A well-known hadith scholar of Albanian origin and Syrian nationality, distinguished in the authentication and grading of hadiths and in hadith jurisprudence.
person/al-alusi-abu-said-al-muayyad: al-Mu'ayyad al-Alusi — famous Iraq poet, chamberlain of al-Mustarshid, then client of the wazir Ibn Hubayra; after a fall he was jailed, and Ibn Khallikan met him in 555 half-blind from the dungeon .
person/al-amash-sulayman-ibn-mihran: A hadith scholar, reciter and expert in inheritance law, nicknamed al-A'mash for weakness of sight.
person/al-amir-fatimid: al-Amir bi-Ahkam Allah Mansur ibn al-Musta'li
Mansur ibn al-Musta'li, tenth Ubaydid caliph as al-Amir bi-Ahkam Allah, raised at five years old on his father's death in 495 .
person/al-anbari-abd-al-rahman: A scholar from al-Anbar on the Euphrates, known as Kamal al-Din.
person/al-anmati-abd-al-wahhab: The Hanbali hafiz Abu al-Barakat Abd al-Wahhab ibn al-Mubarak al-Anmati, mufid of Baghdad; b.
person/al-ansari-al-harawi-abd-allah: Al-Ansari al-Harawi, Abd Allah ibn Muhammad
A memorizer, historian, hadith scholar, Sufi and Qur'an commentator from Herat, a Hanbali who traced his lineage to Abu Ayyub al-Ansari.
person/al-asadi-ahmad-al-sammaki: Meccan scholar of the eleventh century AH who grew up in Mecca.
person/al-ashraf-khalil: al-Malik al-Ashraf Salah al-Din Khalil ibn Qalawun
Qalawun's son; he raised the sidelined caliph — no deed ever asked of him — whose Jumu'a khutba named him to rule and whose jihad khutba urged Baghdad's retaking.
person/al-ashraf-shaban: Mamluk sultan from 764, maker of the ashraf's green turban-badge; betrayed by his amirs on the hajj road in 778, he fled, hid, and was strangled in Dhu'l-Qa'da .
person/al-asmandi-muhammad-ibn-abd-al-ha: A scholar recorded in the biographical dictionaries.
person/al-asmar-abd-al-salam: Libyan Sufi shaykh of Tripoli whose seclusion (khalwa) became known under his name.
person/al-astarabadhi-al-hasan: From Astarabad in Mazandaran; born in 645 AH and died in 715 AH.
person/al-awzai-abd-al-rahman: The imam and foremost jurist of Syria in his time.
person/al-azdi-yahya-ibn-sadun: Andalusi scholar of Cordoba from whom students took hadith.
person/al-aziz-fakhr-al-din-uthman: Al-Malik al-Aziz Fakhr al-Din Uthman — the boy-prince of the Karak line, raised at Baybars' court, then seized on reaching Egypt after the Antioch campaign (666) and held at Qal'at al-Jabal .
person/al-azjani-nasih-al-din-ahmad: Scholar from Arjan in Persia who died in 544 AH.
person/al-baghawi-al-husayn-ibn-muhammad: A hadith scholar and jurist from the town of Baghh in Khurasan, between Marw and Herat.
person/al-baghdadi-abu-ishaq-ibrahim-ibn: al-Baghdadi Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Jabir
Major scholar of the Zahiri legal school, which traces to Dawud ibn Ali al-Isfahani; wrote on the differences among jurists; died 310 AH (922 CE).
person/al-baghdadi-malik-al-nuhat-al-has: al-Baghdadi Malik al-Nuhat al-Hasan ibn Safi
Grammarian, jurist and man of letters of Baghdad, known as the King of Grammarians; born to a freedman father; lived 489–568 AH (1096–1173 CE).
person/al-baji-abu-al-walid-sulayman: Al-Baji, Abu al-Walid Sulayman ibn Khalaf
A hadith scholar, jurist, man of letters, poet, theologian and legal theorist from Beja in al-Andalus, a Maliki.
person/al-baji-muhammad-al-saghir: A Tunisian historian whose full name is often misreported, since he is widely known by the kunya al-Saghir al-Baji.
person/al-bajuri-ibrahim-ibn-muhammad: A Shafi'i theologian and jurist, born in al-Bajur in the Minufiya province of Egypt.
person/al-bakri-abu-ubayd: Al-Bakri, Abu Ubayd Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Aziz
An encyclopaedic scholar of al-Andalus, author of al-Masalik wa-l-Mamalik on geography and history.
person/al-balawi-ahmad-ibn-ali: A philologist, man of letters and poet from Wadi Ash, linked to the tribe of Bali.
person/al-barbahari-al-hasan-ibn-ali: A Hanbali, named after barbahar, a drug imported from India.
person/al-barinbari: Nasir al-Din al-Barinbari (b. ~770) — al-Suyuti's own teacher; taught gratis at the Azhar, lectured, gave fatwas and preached until a stroke paralysed half his body; died Sunday night 11 Rabi' I 832 .
person/al-barqani-ahmad-ibn-muhammad: A Shafi'i jurist from Khwarazm, known as al-Barqani after the village of Barqan near Kath.
person/al-barzali-abu-al-qasim: The jurist and leading scholar of Tunis, author of the large legal compendium al-Diwan al-Kabir.
person/al-barzanji-jafar: Scholar from the Barzanji family of sayyids in Medina, a family known for learning and piety; died 1177 AH.
person/al-bayakandi-ahmad-ibn-ali: A scholar of Bikand, from which he takes his nisba.
person/al-bayduq-abu-bakr-ibn-ali-al-san: al-Bayduq Abu Bakr ibn Ali al-Sanhaji
From the Sanhaja tribe of the central Maghrib, born around 490 AH (1096 CE) and died 555 AH (1160 CE).
person/al-bazdawi-abu-al-yusr-muhammad: Hanafi jurist of Bukhara and judge of Samarqand, to whom the leadership of the Hanafi school passed in his time; died 493 AH (1100 CE).
person/al-bazzar-abu-bakr-ahmad-ibn-amr: al-Bazzar Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Amr
Well-known hadith scholar known as al-Bazzar, who narrated hadith in Isfahan, Baghdad, Egypt and Mecca in his later years; died 292 AH (905 CE).
person/al-bazzar-abu-tahir-abd-al-wahid-: al-Bazzar Abu al-Tahir Abd al-Wahid ibn Umar
Baghdadi reader and grammarian of the late fourth century AH, who died in 349 AH (961 CE); the sources differ on his birth year.
person/al-biqai-ibrahim-ibn-umar: A Shafi'i scholar and hadith specialist from the Biqa' valley, born in 809 AH and died in 885 AH.
person/al-bulaydi-abu-abd-allah-muhammad: al-Bulaydi Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Muhammad
Scholar born in Algeria who moved between the Maghrib, al-Andalus and Tunisia, named after the town of Bulayda; died 1763 CE.
person/al-burshani-ibrahim-ibn-muhammad: Andalusi jurist, linguist and scholar of inheritance law and arithmetic from Wadi Ash (Guadix), who studied with the leading scholars of his time.
person/al-busiri: The poet of the Burda — born near Dalas on Tuesday 1 Shawwal 608, Maghrebi by origin, Busiri by home; the hafiz Ibn Sayyid al-Nas judged him finer than al-Jazzar and al-Warraq .
person/al-busrawi-ala-al-din-ali-ibn-yus: al-Busrawi Ala al-Din Ali ibn Yusuf
Shafi'i jurist of Damascus, a student of Shaykh al-Islam Radi al-Din al-Ghazzi, named after Busra al-Sham; died 1499 CE.
person/al-dakhwar: Muhadhdhib al-Din al-Dakhwar, shaykh of medicine
person/al-dimyati: Abd al-Mu'min ibn Khalaf al-Dimyati, Abu Muhammad, Sharaf al-Din, a hadith hafiz and one of the great Shafi'is; born at Damietta, he died suddenly in Cairo in 705 AH.
person/al-faiz-fatimid: al-Fa'iz bi-Nasr Allah Isa ibn al-Zafir
Isa ibn al-Zafir, thirteenth Ubaydid caliph as al-Fa'iz bi-Nasr Allah — a small boy raised in 549 as Egypt's power failed .
person/al-fakhr-ibn-al-bukhari: al-Fakhr ibn al-Bukhari, musnid of the age
person/al-farabi: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Tarkhan al-Farabi was a philosopher of Turkish origin, born in the district of Farab in Turkestan and called the Second Teacher after Aristotle.
person/al-farawi-kamal-al-din: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abi al-Abbas al-Sa'idi al-Farawi al-Nisaburi, known as Kamal al-Din, jurist and transmitter of hadith.
person/al-fasi-muhammad-ibn-ahmad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Fasi al-Makki (1373–1429), historian and Maliki qadi of Mecca, author of Akhbar Makka.
person/al-firuzabadi: Majd al-Din al-Firuzabadi (1329–1415), Shafi'i lexicographer, author of al-Qamus al-Muhit.
person/al-ghayti-najm-al-din: Najm al-Din al-Ghayti, Egypt's shaykh al-Islam
person/al-ghazali-abu-hamid: Hujjat al-Islam al-Ghazali the Shafi'i, author of the Ihya' — of which al-Nawawi said that were all Islam's books lost and the Ihya' alone remained it would suffice; he died at Tus in 505 .
person/al-hafiz-fatimid: al-Hafiz li-Din Allah Abd al-Majid ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mustansir
Eleventh Ubaydid caliph, raised when his nephew al-Amir was killed heirless in 524; died 544, succeeded by his son al-Zafir .
person/al-hafizi-al-hasan-ibn-ali-ibn-mu: al-Hafizi al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Muhammad
Of the Hafizi family of Rijal Alma in Asir; born 1345 AH (1926 CE) and died 1406 AH (1986 CE).
person/al-hafizi-ibrahim-ibn-ali-zayn-al: al-Hafizi Ibrahim ibn Ali Zayn al-Abidin
Of the Al Bakri al-Ujayli family of Rijal Alma in Asir; born 1305 AH (1888 CE) and died 1372 AH (1952 CE).
person/al-hafizi-muhammad-ibn-ahmad-ibn-: al-Hafizi Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Qadir
Of the Hafizi family, whose lineage links to Shaykh Abu al-Abbas ibn Musa, in Rijal Alma in Asir; born 1176 AH (1762 CE) and died 1237 AH (1821 CE).
person/al-hajj-bashir: The commander whose exploits stood out in Algiers' 948/1541 defence against Charles V's expedition — al-Salabi credits him with cutting down the attackers 'with supreme courage and rare gallantry' .
person/al-halabi-qutb-al-din-abd-al-kari: al-Halabi Qutb al-Din Abd al-Karim ibn Abd al-Nur
Hadith memorist of celebrated standing, of Aleppine origin who settled in Egypt; born 664 AH (1266 CE), died 735 AH (1335 CE).
person/al-halimi-abu-abd-allah-al-husayn: al-Halimi Abu Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan
Scholar of the fourth century AH; born 338 AH (949 CE), died 403 AH (1012 CE).
person/al-hamdani-abu-al-faraj: A poet, prose writer and man of letters born in Nasibin.
person/al-hariri: Al-Hariri of Basra, author of the celebrated Maqamat in which he followed Badi' al-Zaman; his 21st (Raziyya) maqama depicts the preacher Ibn Sam'un .
person/al-hasan-al-alawi-al-murtada: al-Hasan ibn al-Amir Ali al-Murtada al-Alawi
person/al-hasan-ibn-ali-zirid: al-Hasan ibn Ali, last of the Banu Badis
person/al-hasan-ibn-muhammad-al-zafarani: Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah al-Za'farani, one of al-Shafi'i's Baghdadi companions ; he died in 260.
person/al-hasan-ibn-salih-ibn-hayy: Al Hasan Ibn Salih Ibn Hayy
Al-Hasan ibn Salih ibn Hayy — the Zaydi jurist who died in hiding in 168
person/al-haskafi-muhammad-ibn-ali: A Hanafi mufti of Damascus of Hisn origin, author of al-Durr al-Mukhtar on Hanafi law.
person/al-hazimi-muhammad: al-Hazimi al-Hamadhani (548/549–584) — the precise hafiz of Baghdad's east side; traveller through Iraq, Syria, Persia and Azerbaijan; author of al-Nasikh wa-l-Mansukh and Shurut al-A'imma .
person/al-hifnawi-abu-al-makarim-najm-al: al-Hifnawi Abu al-Makarim Najm al-Din Muhammad ibn Salim
Shafi'i jurist of the Khalwati Sufi order, named after Hifna in the Sharqiyya province of Egypt; born 1101 AH (1690 CE) and died 1181 AH (1767 CE).
person/al-hisni-taqi-al-din-abu-bakr-ibn: al-Husni Taqi al-Din Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad
Shafi'i jurist of Damascus, known as al-Husni and called Taqi al-Din; born 752 AH (1351 CE), died 829 AH (1426 CE).
person/al-humaydi-muhammad-ibn-futuh: Historian, man of letters, jurist and hadith scholar who followed the Zahiri school, devoted to learning and asceticism; born 420 AH (1029 CE), died 488 AH (1095 CE).
person/al-husayn-ibn-al-dahhak-al-khali: A poet born and raised in Basra, of Khurasani origin, known as al-Khali' al-Ashqar.
person/al-idrisi-muhammad-ibn-abd-allah: A geographer who wrote Nuzhat al-Mushtaq fi ikhtiraq al-afaq for Roger II, king of Sicily, and completed it in Shawwal 548 AH.
person/al-ifliili-ibrahim-ibn-muhammad: A vizier and an authority on language and literature in al-Andalus, from Cordoba.
person/al-irbili-ahmad-ibn-al-husayn: A scholar from Irbil, one of the learned men of the seventh century AH.
person/al-isfarayini-abu-ishaq-ibrahim: Al-Isfara'ini, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad
A Shafi'i theologian and jurist from Isfara'in, between Nishapur and Gurgan.
person/al-ismaili-abu-bakr-ahmad: Al-Isma'ili, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim
A memorizer and hadith scholar of Jurjan, raised by his father and educated by the scholars of Jurjan.
person/al-isnawi-abd-al-rahim: A Shafi'i jurist from Isna in Upper Egypt.
person/al-istakhri-abu-said-al-hasan: Al-Istakhri, Abu Sa'id al-Hasan ibn Ahmad
One of the Shafi'i authorities of Baghdad and judge of Qumm; named after Istakhr in Fars.
person/al-itqani: Amir Katib ibn Amir Umar ibn Amir Ghazi, Qawam al-Din Abu Hanifa al-Itqani al-Farabi, a leader of the Hanafi school, skilled in law, Arabic and other sciences.
person/al-iylani-muzaffar: Muzaffar al-Din al-Iylani, the blind prosodist
person/al-izz-ibn-abd-al-ghani: Al-Izz Muhammad, Abu al-Fath, son of the hafiz Abd al-Ghani ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Maqdisi, himself a hafiz and son of a hafiz.
person/al-jabali-ibrahim-hasan-ibn-yusuf: Scholar and writer of al-Azhar, born in al-Rahmaniyya in the Beheira province of Egypt in 1295 AH (1878 CE); died 1370 AH (1951 CE).
person/al-jabari-abu-ishaq-ibrahim-ibn-u: al-Ju'bari Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Umar
Reader of the Qur'an known in Baghdad as Taqi al-Din and elsewhere as Burhan al-Din; died 732 AH (1332 CE).
person/al-jaghmini-mahmud-ibn-muhammad-i: Among the scientific pioneers of Anatolia within Islamic civilisation, named after the village of Jaghmin; died 618 AH (1220 CE).
person/al-jahiz: Abu Uthman Amr ibn Bahr al-Jahiz was a man of letters from Basra and a famous Arab prose writer, who wrote on adab, Mu'tazili theology and politico-religious polemics.
person/al-janadari-ahmad-ibn-abd-allah: A Yemeni scholar, known as al-Janadari after the town of al-Janad.
person/al-jawaliqi-abu-mansur-mawhub-ibn: al-Jawaliqi Abu Mansur Mawhub ibn Ahmad
Baghdadi philologist and man of letters, born and raised in Baghdad, named after the Persian word jawaliq meaning justice; died 540 AH (1145 CE).
person/al-jawzajani-ibrahim-ibn-yaqub: A hadith scholar from Jawzjan, named after Bushanj.
person/al-jayyani-al-husayn-ibn-muhammad: Imam, hadith memorist and traditionist of al-Andalus, named after Jaen where his father lived for a time, of Madinat al-Zahra origin; died 498 AH (1105 CE).
person/al-jazari-engineer: An engineer and author on mechanical devices, identified by TDV as an Islamic scholar serving the Artuqids at Amid in 1181–1206.
person/al-jubbai: Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab ibn Salam ibn Khalid al-Jubba'i, one of the imams of the Mu'tazila; he was an imam in kalam and the leading theologian of his age.
person/al-jundi-ali-al-sayyid: Man of letters, poet and professor of Arabic literature, dean of Dar al-Ulum and member of the Arabic Language Academy; born 1316 AH (1898 CE), died 1393 AH (1973 CE).
person/al-jurayri-al-maafa-ibn-zakariyya: A scholar from Nahrawan, known as al-Jurayri and Ibn Tarar, who wrote on language and hadith.
person/al-kamal-al-darir: Shaykh of the qurra' — al-Shatibi's own companion and son-in-law (b.
person/al-kamal-al-fuwayra: Musnid of Iraq and shaykh of the Mustansiriyya; he read the readings with al-Fakhr al-Mawsili, and the highest chains of transmission in the readings and in hadith ended with him.
person/al-kamal-al-mahalli: Cairo's blind shaykh of the qurra' — holder of the western-iwan hadith chair at the newly finished Zahiriyya (662); d.
person/al-kamal-al-suyuti: al-Kamal Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, father of al-Suyuti
The author's father, imam to caliph al-Mustakfi II — held in highest honour, writer of his deed of appointment — who outlived his caliph by only forty days .
person/al-kawkabani-1756: Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Qadir al-Kawkabani (1756–1808), Zaydi jurist of San'a, author of fiqh treatises and tender verse.
person/al-khalil-ibn-ahmad-al-farahidi: One of the greatest scholars of Arabic, of the Azd of Oman, raised in Basra.
person/al-khalili-abu-ya-la-al-khalil-ib: al-Khalili Abu Ya'la al-Khalil ibn Abd Allah
Hadith scholar, born about 370 AH (980 CE, estimated) and died 446 AH (1055 CE).
person/al-khasruwshahi: The Shafi'i mutakallim of Khasruwshah near Marw (b.
person/al-khayali-ahmad-ibn-musa-shams-a: al-Khayali Ahmad ibn Musa Shams al-Din
Theologian of the creed, a Rumi Hanafi and pupil of Khidr Bik; taught at the Sultan's madrasa in Bursa and then at Iznik; died there in 862 AH (1458 CE).
person/al-khunaji: The Shafi'i qadi al-qudat and logician (b.
person/al-khunaji-afdal-al-din-muhammad: Scholar of medicine, philosophy and logic of Persian origin; born 590 AH (1194 CE) and died 646 AH (1248 CE).
person/al-khuwayyi-abu-al-abbas-shams-al: al-Khuwayyi Abu al-Abbas Shams al-Din Ahmad
Lived about fifty-five years, died in Hebron and was buried there in 637 AH (1240 CE).
person/al-khwarazmi-abu-bakr-muhammad-ib: al-Khwarazmi Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Abbas
Born in Khwarazm in 323 AH (935 CE); travelled widely in pursuit of learning and wealth; died 382 AH (993 CE).
person/al-khwarizmi: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi was a mathematician, astronomer and geographer who worked in the House of Wisdom in Baghdad under al-Ma'mun, and al-Mas'udi numbered him among Islam's astronomers .
person/al-kindi-abu-al-yumn: The alim Taj al-Din Abu al-Yumn Zayd ibn al-Hasan ibn Zayd ibn al-Hasan al-Baghdadi, reader, grammarian and philologist; shaykh of the readers and grammarians in Syria and musnid of his age.
person/al-kiya-al-harrasi-ali-ibn-muhamm: One of the leading Shafi'i authorities in jurisprudence, legal theory and disputation, and in memorizing the texts of hadiths on rulings.
person/al-kughiri: Shams al-Din al-Kughiri (b. 757) — famed for memorized furu', qadi al-rakb, compiler of a six-volume commentary on al-Bukhari plus 'Ayn al-Bahiyya and Zahr al-Rawd; died 13 Muharram 831 .
person/al-kurani-al-harawi: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Abd al-Salam al-Kurani al-Harawi, a man of letters of distinction in memorising ancient and modern poetry, in which he excelled.
person/al-maafiri-muhammad: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Ma'afiri al-Andalusi al-Ishbili, the well-known hafiz.
person/al-mahani: Al-Mahani — geometer of the calculator school
person/al-malik-al-adil-ayyub: al-Malik al-Adil Sayf al-Din Abu Bakr ibn Ayyub
Salah al-Din's brother; when al-Aziz died in 595 leaving the boy al-Mansur, al-Adil seized Egypt then placed his son al-Kamil over it .
person/al-malik-al-adil-salamish: Baybars's son — sultan for three months after al-Sa'id's deposition, then set aside; al-Ashraf Khalil shipped him and his brother al-Khidr to Constantinople, where he died at about twenty .
person/al-malik-al-afdal-ali: al-Malik al-Afdal Nur al-Din Ali ibn Salah al-Din
Salah al-Din's son; Damascus settled for him in 589 .
person/al-malik-al-ashraf: The Ayyubid lord of Damascus who ordered the Ashrafiyya dar al-hadith in 628, finished in 630 .
person/al-malik-al-awhad-karak: Lord of Karak from the house of Ayyub, son of al-Nasir Dawud; he heard from Ibn al-Lati, and al-Dimyati transmitted from him in his Mu'jam, and he died in Jerusalem in Dhu'l-Hijja, aged seventy .
person/al-malik-al-kamil: al-Malik al-Kamil Muhammad ibn al-Adil ibn Ayyub
Ayyubid sultan, set over Egypt by his father al-Adil in 595; when the Franks took Damietta in 616 he founded al-Mansura at the seas' fork and camped there .
person/al-malik-al-mansur-hajji: He succeeded his uncle al-Nasir Hasan in Jumada I 762, with Yalbugha directing his state; Yalbugha travelled with him to Syria when he was about fifteen.
person/al-malik-al-mansur-ii-hama: Hama's last long Ayyubid — enthroned at ten in 642 under his mother's regency and ruling some forty years; al-'Ibar's terse verdict: 'an insistent gamester — may God pardon him' .
person/al-malik-al-mushammar: al-Malik al-Zafir, known as al-Mushammar, Muzaffar al-Din, son of Sultan Salah al-Din Yusuf ibn Ayyub and brother of al-Malik al-Afdal.
person/al-malik-al-nasir-salah-al-din-da: Al-Malik al-Nasir Salah al-Din Dawud b.
person/al-malik-al-qahir-masud: Lord of Mosul, Sultan al-Malik al-Qahir Izz al-Din Abu'l-Fath Mas'ud, son of Sultan Nur al-Din Arslan Shah ibn Mas'ud al-Atabegi al-Zengi.
person/al-malik-al-salih-ayyub: al-Malik al-Salih Najm al-Din Ayyub ibn al-Kamil
Ayyubid sultan of Egypt, builder of the madrasa between the palaces and the Rawda citadel; he died mid-Sha'ban 647 as the Franks took Damietta, Shajar al-Durr hiding his death .

Salah al-Din's son; Aleppo settled for him in 589 .

person/al-mawardi: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Mawardi al-Shafi'i, d.

person/al-muazzam-turanshah-al-kabir: The grand old man of the Ayyubid house (b.

person/al-muhibb-mufid-al-jabal: The Maqdisi hafiz (d. 12 Jumada II 658, aged 40) — pupil of al-Muwaffaq, traveller to Baghdad for the Qabiti and Ibn al-Fakhar; 'most complete in his devotion to hadith' .
person/al-mujir-al-wasiti: Al-Mujir the imam Abu al-Qasim Mahmud b.
person/al-muqaddasi: Shams al-Din Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Muqaddasi (al-Bishshari, d.

Abbasid caliph [467–487], posthumous son of the Qa'im's son Muhammad, born six months after his father's death and hailed at nineteen before Abu Ishaq al-Shirazi.
person/al-muqtafi-billah: al-Muqtafi li-Amr Allah Muhammad ibn al-Mustazhir
Abbasid caliph [530–555], hailed at forty when his nephew was deposed — his laqab from a dream of the Prophet bidding him 'follow my steps'.
person/al-mustadi-billah: al-Mustadi bi-Amr Allah al-Hasan ibn al-Mustanjid
person/al-mustakfi-billah: Third Cairo caliph [701–740], hailed by his father's will; moved with the Abbasids from Kabsh to a citadel house, and rode out with the sultan to the Tatar victory of 702 .
person/al-mustakfi-i-cairo: al-Mustakfi I, the caliph of the Abbasid of Cairo caliphate, ruling 1303–1340 CE.

person/al-mustanjid-billah: Abbasid caliph [555–566]; he lifted Iraq's tolls and was hard on mischief-makers — to the man offering ten thousand dinars for a prisoner he answered 'take them, and show me another like him to jail'.
person/al-mustansir-billah: Abbasid caliph [623–640], hailed Rajab 623; builder of the Mustansiriyya — four madhhab chairs, bimaristan, kitchen, hammam, 70,000-mithqal waqf.
person/al-mustansir-fatimid: Ma'add ibn al-Zahir, eighth Ubaydid caliph, enthroned at seven in 428 and reigning sixty years and four months — al-Dhahabi knows none in Islam who lasted so.

person/al-mutarrizi: Nasir al-Din al-Mutarrizi, born in 538 AH (1143) at Jurjaniyya, capital of Khwarazm, and died there on 8 October 1213.
person/al-mutawakkil-ala-llah-ii: al-Mutawakkil ala Allah II, Abd al-Aziz ibn Ya'qub
Cairo caliph [884–903] — a Hashimi between Hashimis, who read hadith with the author's father; hailed in the sultan's presence 16 Muharram 884.
person/al-muzaffar-ibn-al-aftas: al-Muzaffar ibn al-Aftas, king of Badajoz
person/al-najirmi: Abu Ya'qub Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn Isma'il ibn Kharrazadh al-Najirmi, the Basran philologist who settled in Egypt.
person/al-naqqash-al-muqri: al-Naqqash (265/266–351) — the Baghdadi qari' and exegete of Mosuli origin; author of Shifa' al-Sudur and three mu'jams on the readers and their readings; al-Barqani dismissed his hadith as munkar .
person/al-nasai: Abu Abd al-Rahman Ahmad ibn Shu'ayb al-Nasa'i, a muhaddith from Nasa in Khurasan, was born in 215/830 and compiled the Sunan, one of the six canonical hadith collections.
person/al-nasir-billah: al-Nasir li-Din Allah Ahmad ibn al-Mustadi'
Abbasid caliph [575–622], longest reign of any — forty-seven years.
person/al-nasir-hasan: al-Nasir Hasan, Mamluk sultan of Egypt

person/al-nasir-muhammad-ibn-qalawun: Mamluk sultan thrice fated: raised at nine in 693, deposed for Kitbugha then Lajin, restored from Karak's exile in 698 with the caliph's investiture .
person/al-nasir-yusuf: Damascus's lord, to whom Hulagu sent the three dread letters after Baghdad's fall .

person/al-qadi-al-fadil: al-Qadi al-Fadil Abd al-Rahim al-Baysani (535–596) — Salah al-Din's chancellor of correspondence, master of insha'; built a madrasa at Darb Malukhiya; Ibn Khallikan visited his grave at Muqattam .
person/al-qaim-billah: al-Qa'im bi-Amr Allah Abd Allah ibn al-Qadir
Abbasid caliph [422–467], Abu Ja'far Abd Allah ibn al-Qadir, born 391 to an Armenian mother; Ibn al-Athir praises his beauty, piety, learning and unstinted answers.
person/al-qasim-ibn-asakir: Al-Qasim ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Hibat Allah, Abu Muhammad, Ibn Asakir, a hadith scholar of Damascus and son of the author of the great history; 527 to 600 AH.
person/al-qasim-ibn-muhammad: The Prophet's eldest son by Khadija, from whom his kunya Abu al-Qasim derives; he died young in Mecca.
person/al-qastallani-shihab-al-din: The hafiz of Bukhari's greatest sharh — b.
person/al-qatiqi: Ahmad b. Ja'far Abu Bakr al-Qati'i (274–368), the Baghdad muhaddith named for Qati'at al-Daqiq where he lived; he transmitted 'Abd Allah b.
person/al-qaysari: Al-Qaysari, a Shafi'i jurist whom Ibn al-Salah counted among the leading scholars of Iraq.
person/al-qaysi-al-dimashqi: Damascus adib — companion and transmitter of Ibn Khalil, insha'-scribe for al-Adil then Baybars; d.
person/al-quduri: Abu al-Husayn al-Quduri Ahmad ibn Muhammad
person/al-qurashi-jamal-al-din-muhammad-: Jamal al-Din al-Qurashi Muhammad ibn Umar

person/al-raffaqi-al-husayn-ibn-muhammad: A man of letters from al-Raqqa, with the kunya Abu Abd Allah.

person/al-sadid-ibn-makki: The last companion of hafiz Ibn Asakir to die (Safar 652, aged 89) — sole transmitter also from Ibn al-Khaldun the elder .
person/al-sadr-al-bakri: The Sufi hafiz (b. 574, d. 656) — of Nishapur then Damascus; heard at Mecca, Damascus, Khurasan and Isfahan .
person/al-safawi-sayyid: The Iji grandson — b. 900, grandson of Safi al-Din al-Iji the mufassir; trained at Delhi's majalis under Sultan Ibrahim b.
person/al-sakkaki: Siraj al-Din al-Sakkaki, author of al-Miftah
person/al-salah-ibn-uthman: Al-Salah Abd al-Rahman b. Uthman al-Shahrazuri (b.
person/al-salami-muhammad: Al-Salami (336–393) — the Makhzumi poet of Baghdad, descended from al-Walid b.
person/al-salih-salah-al-din-ahmad: Al-Malik al-Salih Salah al-Din Ahmad (600–651) — Ayyubid lord of Ayntab, elder brother of al-Aziz of Aleppo, passed over for the succession because his mother was a concubine .
person/al-samiri-ibn-sinina: Abu Abdallah Nasir al-Din Muhammad ibn Abdallah ibn al-Husayn al-Samiri, the Hanbali jurist and expert in inheritance law, known as Ibn Sinina.
person/al-sarkhasi-abu-al-faraj: Abu al-Faraj al-Zaz al-Sarkhasi, jurist of Marw
Abu al-Faraj 'al-Zaz' al-Sarkhasi Abd al-Rahman b.
person/al-saymari-al-husayn: al-Saymari, Abu Abdallah al-Husayn ibn Ali
The Hanafi qadi of Baghdad — born 351, a jurist of fine expression and sound reasoning who judged al-Mada'in then the Karkh quarter; among the jurists who permitted the 'malik al-muluk' laqab in 429.
person/al-sayyid-al-nassaba: Al-Sayyid Husayn (b. Salihiyya 774) — shaykh of Damascus's shaykhs and its genealogist, who 'claimed to have compiled five books on nasab'; died Sha'ban 866 past one hundred .
person/al-sayyida-nafisa: Nafisa bt. al-Hasan b. Zayd b. al-Hasan b.

person/al-shamunni: Ahmad al-Shamunni (1399–1468), Alexandrian hadith scholar, mufassir and grammarian of Constantine origin.

person/al-sharif-al-jurjani-ali-ibn-muha: A scholar of philosophy, logic, theology and rhetoric, born in Taju and known as al-Sharif al-Jurjani.
person/al-sharishi: The Andalusi Maliki of Sharish (Jerez, b.

person/al-shaykh-al-imad: Al-Shaykh al-Imad Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Maqdisi al-Hanbali, brother of the hafiz Abd al-Ghani.
person/al-shaykhi-ali-ibn-muhammad: A Baghdadi scholar of jurisprudence and hadith in the eighth century AH.
person/al-shihab-al-qusi: Shafi'i ra'is and wakil of Syria's bayt al-mal (b.

person/al-shirazi-faqih: Ibrahim ibn Ali al-Shirazi “Abu Ishaq” (1003–1083), Shafi'i jurist and chief of the Baghdad Nizamiyya, author of al-Muhadhdhab.
person/al-sini: Author of al-Aghani on alphabetical order for al-Mutawakkil
person/al-sukraji: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Karaji al-Sukraji
person/al-suyuti: Jalal al-Din Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Suyuti (849-911 AH); Egypt's prolific hadith imam, author among much else of Tarikh al-Khulafa, caliphal biographies to his own day.
person/al-tabari: Al-Tabari — b. 224 at Amul, d. Shawwal 310 at 87; the Fihrist's account of his teachers, his own madhhab and his books
person/al-tabarsi: Al-Fadl ibn al-Hasan al-Tabarsi, Amin al-Din, Abu Ali, an Imami scholar, exegete and linguist with a nisba to Tabaristan; author of Majma' al-Bayan; died in Sabzevar in 548 AH (1153 CE).
person/al-tabbakh: Shams al-Din al-Tabbakh the Meccan sharif

person/al-talafari-abu-al-makarim-muhamm: al-Tala'fari Abu al-Makarim Muhammad ibn Yusuf

person/al-tanasi-muhammad-ibn-abd-allah: A memorizing scholar from Tlemcen, probably born in Madin.

person/al-tanukhi-al-qadi-abu-al-qasim-a: al-Tanukhi al-Qadi Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn al-Muhsin
Judge Abu al-Qasim Ali ibn al-Muhsin al-Tanukhi, companion and pupil of Abu al-Ala al-Ma'arri; died 474 AH (1081 CE).
person/al-taqi-al-bayyi: al-Taqi al-Bayyi', vizier to five sultans

person/al-tartushi: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Walid ibn Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Fihri al-Andalusi al-Tartushi, the Maliki jurist and ascetic known as Ibn Abi Randaqa.
person/al-tattai-muhammad-ibn-ibrahim: A Maliki jurist, author of Tanwir al-Maqala on Maliki law.

person/al-thaqafi-al-jayyani-muhammad-ib: Preacher, reader, hadith scholar and man of letters of Jaen in al-Andalus, who travelled through the southern cities; died 663 AH (1264 CE).
person/al-thumami-abu-al-hasan-abd-al-az: al-Thumami Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Harith
One of the leading Hanbali scholars of law, legal theory and inheritance, of the Tamim tribe; died 371 AH (982 CE).
person/al-tijibi-al-sabti-abu-al-qasim-i: al-Tujibi al-Sabti Abu al-Qasim ibn Yusuf

person/al-tilimsani-al-sharif-muhammad-i: Imam of the Maghrib and a leading figure of the Maliki school, born in Tlemcen in 710 AH (1310 CE); died 771 AH (1370 CE).

person/al-tizini-muhammad-ibn-muhammad: Hanafi astronomer and mathematician of Aleppo, named after the town of Tizin near Aleppo; born 828 AH (1424 CE), died 911 AH (1505 CE).

person/al-udfawi: Ja'far al-Udfawi (1286–1347), Egyptian historian and littérateur of Edfu, author of al-Tali' al-Sa'id.

person/al-zaki-al-barzali: al-Zaki al-Barzali (d. Ramadan 636, Hama) — 'muhaddith al-Sham wa-mufiduhu', the Sevillan who began his rihla in 512 and heard from Isfahan to the Jazira; father of Alam al-Din al-Barzali .
person/ala-al-din-muhammad-iii-nizari: Ala al-Din Muhammad III of Alamut

person/alboury-ndaye: Alboury Ndiaye (c. 1848 – 1901), the last Buurba (king) of an independent Jolof in present-day Senegal, famed for his determined resistance to the French conquest.
person/alexander-russell-webb: American journalist, publisher and diplomat (1846–1916), United States consul at Manila, who embraced Islam in 1888 (one source says 1887) and is among the first prominent Americans to do so.
person/alfonso-vi-castile: Alfonso VI of León and Castile

person/ali-al-hadi: The 'Alid raided at night on a slander and found alone in a hair-cloth house of sand and gravel chanting the verses of promise — then honoured by al-Mutawakkil after the 'Abbas riposte .

person/ali-ibn-umar-al-qazwini: Ibn al-Qazwini the ascetic (Ali ibn Umar al-Harbi)

person/ali-ibn-uthman-al-awsi: Ali ibn Uthman ibn Muhammad, Siraj al-Din al-Awsi al-Farghani, a scholar, man of letters and poet.
person/ali-khan: Indian musician and Sufi teacher (1881–1958), born in Baroda and died in The Hague.
person/ali-mitayev: Ali Bamat-Gireyevich Mitayev (1881–1925) was a Chechen Sufi sheikh and political and military leader.
person/ali-shariati: Iranian sociologist and thinker (1933–1977), among the most influential intellectuals before the Iranian revolution.
person/alija-izetbegovic: Bosnian politician, philosopher and author, born in 1925.
person/alladiya-khan: Indian classical singer (1855–1946), born at Uniara in Jaipur State into a family of musicians.

person/allal-al-fassi: Moroccan scholar, jurist and politician (1910–1974), born at Fez and formed at the Qarawiyyin.
